clue.text: Cash to start business in empty apartment

indicators.note: in tells us the empty-looking letter sits inside the word for a flat

parts.note: an apartment is a flat
something empty is a zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone launches a company from a bare, unfurnished flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' looks like it describes the apartment, but it gives O, the zero shape, which goes 'in' FLAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A float is the sum of ready money put into a new venture or a till at the outset.

clue.text: Anticipate warning on course to stable

parts.note: fore is the shout a golfer gives on a golf course
a stall is a stable or compartment for a horse

explanation.surface: A golfer predicts the shout of warning on the way to the horse's quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: FORE is the warning shouted on a golf course; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To act first and so prevent something is to get in ahead of it, which is anticipating it.

clue.text: Happen to find cold old dog outside

indicators.note: outside says the old dog surrounds the abbreviation for cold

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
C is cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles on a shivering elderly mutt out of doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old dog' makes O and CUR, and 'outside' wraps them round C; 'to find' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To occur is to take place, a synonym of happen.

clue.text: Drinker's one paying extra — about a pound

definitions.note: the definition with 's, read as drinker is

indicators.note: about means the extra-payer goes round the pound sign

parts.note: a tipper pays extra for good service
L is the pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A heavy drinker is someone who leaves generous tips of around a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside TIPPER, between the P and E; the 's on the definition means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tippler is a habitual drinker of alcohol.

clue.text: Device for connecting sound with incomplete working keyboard

parts.note: sound in the sense of secure and unharmed means safe

indicators.note: incomplete says the word for keyboard work loses its final letter

parts.note: working a keyboard is typing

explanation.surface: A gadget that links a speaker to a half-finished computer keyboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' cuts the last letter G from TYPING, leaving TYPIN; 'with' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A fastening pin with a guarded point is used to join pieces of cloth together.

clue.text: Money that's produced after mushrooms come up

indicators.note: after puts the piece for that's following the turned mushrooms
come up in a down clue means the mushroom word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: ceps are a kind of edible mushroom
that's means that is, abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: Cash generated once the mushroom crop has sprouted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come up' turns the mushrooms in this down clue; 'produced' is only a link, and 'that's' is the everyday abbreviation for 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Specie is money in the form of coins rather than notes.

clue.text: Army punishment some scoff at. I guess

indicators.note: some says only part of the following words is wanted

explanation.surface: A soldier's penalty that some people mock, the speaker supposes.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'at. I' where the held text has a stray quote mark. The letters run on from scofF AT I GUESs.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatigues are menial duties given to soldiers, often as a punishment.

clue.text: With insect, was first to have caught trout

parts.note: a tick is a small bloodsucking creature, loosely called an insect
to lead is to be first, past tense led

explanation.surface: An angler using a bug as bait was the first to land a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' and 'to have' are links. Trout can be caught by stroking their bellies by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Trout tickling is a poacher's method of catching the fish by hand.

clue.text: Many call for shares in this political programme

definitions.text: Many call for shares in this
definitions.meaning: a telephone line shared by several subscribers, which many people call on
the official policy a political party expects its members to follow

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers both a shared phone line and a party's official policy stance.

clue.text: Drain off at the lowest point

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to empty a tank at the bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges DRAIN; 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the bottom-most point, the opposite of the zenith.

clue.text: He gets single insertion in guide to cookery books

indicators.note: insertion in signals one piece being placed within the cookery guide

parts.note: a recipe is a guide to cooking a dish
single is one, the Roman numeral I
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone receives a lone extra page inserted in a cookbook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He gets' is the definition: a receiver. 'insertion in' puts the single letter just before the final E of the cookery guide.
explanation.definitionFit: A recipient is a person who receives something, so he gets it.

clue.text: Made runs but after opener's dismissal lost heart

indicators.note: the cricket opener being dismissed is the first letter going, so the synonym loses its initial

parts.note: in cricket, making runs is scoring

explanation.surface: A cricketer made runs, but once the opening batsman was out, the team's spirit sank.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an opener is the first batsman in; here 'opener' is the first letter S of SCORED, which is dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit that is cored has had its centre removed, so it has lost its middle.

clue.text: Does such an actor never enjoy a run?

definitions.text: Does such an actor never enjoy a run?

parts.words: Does such an actor never enjoy a run?
parts.note: a touring actor of old moved from town to town, so he never stayed for a long theatrical run, though he was always walking on

explanation.surface: A wry question about a performer who never gets a long stint on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: A run is a long series of performances of one show; a touring player keeps moving instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Itinerant actors who wandered between towns performing were known by this name.

clue.text: Dawn showing through skylights

definitions.meaning: the Roman goddess of the dawn, and so daybreak itself
the coloured lights in the polar night sky, read as a display seen in the sky's lights

explanation.definitionFit: The Latin name for daybreak is also given to the shimmering polar light displays.

clue.text: Came home to roost in spring, settling in the long grass

indicators.note: settling in says the spring word comes to rest inside the grass word

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass growing by water
a spring or leap is a bound

explanation.surface: Birds returning to nest in springtime settle among tall grasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season but is a leap; 'settling in' tucks it among the grass, and the first 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: When something comes home to roost it recoils on the one who caused it, as a ball bounces back.

clue.text: A frontal blow that takes one aback

definitions.text: A frontal blow that takes one aback

parts.words: A frontal blow that takes one aback
parts.note: a wind blowing straight at the front of a ship or plane, pushing it backwards rather than shocking a person

explanation.surface: A punch in the face that leaves someone stunned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken aback' is a sailing term for sails pressed back by wind from ahead, as well as meaning surprised.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind that blows directly against the direction of travel, from in front.

clue.text: Fellow's put in fitting accommodation, having propensity to break out

indicators.note: put in means the fellow's word is placed inside the word for fitting

parts.note: decent accommodation is suitable, fitting lodging
a fellow's things are his

explanation.surface: A man is housed in suitable lodgings but is liable to escape.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is botanical: seed pods that split open are said to burst out, and 'Fellow's' gives the possessive word, not a fellow plus S.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany a dehiscent pod or fruit splits open naturally to release its seeds.

clue.text: It is responsible for revolution in cookery

definitions.text: It is responsible for revolution in cookery

parts.words: It is responsible for revolution in cookery
parts.note: not a culinary upheaval but a device, or kitchen boy, that turned a roasting skewer round and round

explanation.surface: Something that brought about a radical change in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' suggests a sweeping change but means turning round.
explanation.definitionFit: A roasting jack or servant that rotated meat over the fire on a spit.

clue.text: Source of wood that could produce a fire in chimney

indicators.note: in tells us the fire phrase sits inside the Scots chimney word

parts.note: lum is a Scots word for a chimney
to fire something is to burn it

explanation.surface: Kindling that might start a blaze up the flue.
explanation.walkthrough: The chimney word is Scots and northern English; 'that could produce' is a link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: This small tree with yellow hanging flowers yields a hard, dark timber.

clue.text: Russian company volunteers to get rise for old soldier

parts.note: red was the colour of Soviet communism, so a Russian

indicators.note: get rise in a down clue means the volunteers' letters go upwards, read in reverse

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A Russian firm's volunteers win promotion in place of a veteran.
explanation.walkthrough: TA, the Territorial Army of volunteers, read upwards is AT. 'to' and 'for' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Redcoats were British soldiers of past centuries, named after their scarlet tunics.

clue.text: Welshman making potentially great husband

indicators.note: potentially suggests what the word great could become if its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man from Wales shaping up as a fine spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potentially' rearranges GREAT into GARET, and 'making' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This given name is a typically Welsh one, so it stands for a man from Wales.

clue.text: Pull up vehicle in a race

indicators.note: in places the turned vehicle within the race letters

parts.note: the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the vehicle word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a cart is a simple vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone stops a car in the middle of a motor race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull up' looks like stopping, but 'up' belongs to the wordplay, turning the vehicle so it reads TRAC in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To attract is to draw something towards you, which is to pull it.

clue.text: Go astray from start to finish

parts.note: the off is the start of a race
the end is the finish

explanation.surface: Getting lost all the way through a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To offend is to transgress or sin, which is going astray morally.

clue.text: Suffering had not broken, these early American settlers

indicators.note: broken means the letters of the preceding words are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: Hardship never crushed the first colonists of America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not broken' reads as one idea, but 'broken' is the anagram signal for all three words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used for the statesmen behind the US Constitution and also for the Pilgrim colonists.

clue.text: Class assembled round university meeting place

indicators.note: round says the class word goes about the university letter

parts.note: a form is a school class gathered together

explanation.surface: Students gather around a college building where people meet.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a school year group is called a form.
explanation.definitionFit: A forum was the public square of a Roman town, a place for assembly.

clue.text: Duck heading off gull

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter of the deceive word is removed

parts.note: to gull someone is to deceive or delude them

explanation.surface: A duck chases away a seagull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gull' is a verb, to fool. 'heading off' removes the D from DELUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck a question or a blow is to avoid or dodge it.

clue.text: Took horses to ring for cowboy display

parts.note: to take horses out is to ride them, past tense rode
a ring is round, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone led horses into an arena for a western show.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodeo is an exhibition of cowboy skills such as bronco riding and roping.

clue.text: Hasty withdrawal of animal trainer in simple enclosure

indicators.note: in places the turned trainer inside the word for simple

parts.note: simple means pure, unmixed

indicators.note: withdrawal suggests drawing back, so the trainer word is read backwards

parts.note: a tamer trains wild animals

explanation.surface: A lion tamer pulls out of a basic cage too soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawal of' turns the trainer round to give REMAT; 'Hasty' is the definition, as a premature act is a hasty one.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done prematurely happens too soon, which is acting in haste.

clue.text: Considered getting married — sort out the papers after the 1st

annotationWithheld.why: Considered getting married — sort out the papers after the 1st (9): M for married plus EDIT for sort out leaves ATED, and no reading of 'the papers after the 1st' gives those letters.
annotationWithheld.clue: Considered getting married — sort out the papers after the 1st

clue.text: Negotiate for doctor or nurse

definitions.meaning: to negotiate terms, to deal with another party
used as verbs: to give medical care to a patient

explanation.definitionFit: One verb covers bargaining with someone and caring for an illness medically.
